gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 recognizes the separate lack of time regularity needed to define the derivative-based estimator and apply the stronger reliability hypothesis. It does not recognize the additional gold defect that endpoint evaluation of general L2 equivalence-class data makes the scheme itself undefined, nor the associated need for meshwise projected data and a re-established projected-data theory. The shared forcing-data setting is insufficient for full coverage.

The gold issue concerns unsupported spectral and self-adjointness assumptions used to construct an orthonormal eigenbasis and perform the modewise inf-sup argument. ISSUE-002 concerns differentiability of the forcing and applicability of an estimator reliability lemma; it supplies no diagnosis of the operator's spectral hypotheses or eigenfunction expansion.

Both entries identify the same false mesh- and eigenvalue-uniform equivalence between the invisible quadratic mode's endpoint values and its L2/X norm. ISSUE-001 supplies the large-|T|lambda construction showing vanishing residual tests with growing norm, which is the gold counterexample to the inf-sup claim, and its repair addresses the corresponding initial-trace and corrected stability formulation.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof falsely treats right-endpoint values of the invisible quadratic mode as controlling its element L2/X norm, so the unrestricted full-space inf-sup lower bound fails for large |T|lambda and requires initial-trace-aware stability.

component_coverage.gold_component: The asserted right-endpoint norm equivalence for invisible quadratic modes is false, yielding failure of the unrestricted mesh- and eigenvalue-uniform inf-sup estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same quadratic q_T, endpoint asymptotics, vanishing test residual, norm growth, and resulting failure of the uniform inf-sup constant, and proposes controlling the invisible boundary-layer mode.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify that full-space errors are generally not reduced-valued, so applying the reduced-space X_R norm to them is undefined or ill-typed. The prediction also recognizes the required correction: use a norm defined on the full space or an appropriate ambient norm rather than the reduced norm.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The reduced-basis error theorem applies X_R^(rb) to quantities with components outside the reduced space, so its norm comparison is not well-formed; an ambient/full-space error norm is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: The reduced-space norm is applied to full-space solution and projection errors that do not belong to the reduced space, invalidating the basic and dependent MOR bounds.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that the total and projection errors are not reduced-valued, their reduced norms are undefined, and they must instead be measured with a norm defined on X_h or another ambient full space.
